_header: Retrieval cases over README.md, DECISIONS.md and docs/*.md. THE LABELS WERE WRITTEN BY A MODEL, NOT BY A PERSON: the model read the documents and wrote each question, the sections that answer it and the key facts. No person has checked them. Every figure computed from this file is a score against a model's labels. Fields: id; question; split (dev or test, drawn by evalkit.retrieval.assign_split with a fixed seed); relevant (section ids, file#heading, any of which answers the question); key_facts (what an answer must contain: fact is the statement, any_of the lowercase strings of which at least one must appear in the answer).

question: Why are 2026-08-09 and 2026-09-25 partial days in the data?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The twelve template families
DECISIONS.md#15. The external comparison only looks at days that are whole on both sides

key_facts.fact: the backfill window starts and ends inside a day, so the first and last day hold part of a day
the evaluation draws complete days only, 2026-08-10 to 2026-09-24

question: What is net volume?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#18. Round trips are measured, not removed

key_facts.fact: it is the volume without the legs of round trips
gross volume is volume_usd and net is net_volume_usd, side by side
it is in fct_pool_daily_round_trips

question: Why does fct_pool_daily.volume_usd still include round trips?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#18. Round trips are measured, not removed

key_facts.fact: the gross figure is what an external source reports and what the reconciliation compares
removing the legs would open a difference with every source

question: How is a round trip defined?
relevant: docs/ROUND_TRIPS.md#The definition
DECISIONS.md#18. Round trips are measured, not removed

key_facts.fact: same pool, same block, same sender
the second swap comes later in the block and moves the non-stable leg the opposite way
it undoes 90% to 110% of the first (within 10%)

question: Why does the project use plain JSON-RPC over requests and not web3.py?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#3. Plain JSON-RPC over `requests`, not web3.py

key_facts.fact: only two methods are needed, eth_blockNumber and eth_getLogs
chunking, retries and the checkpoint are controlled by hand
decoding the Swap event by hand, including signed int256 two's complement

question: Why is the ClickHouse memory ceiling 2.70 GiB when mem_limit is 3g?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#6. A hard 3 GiB memory limit with no swap, and what ClickHouse does with it

key_facts.fact: the server reads the cgroup limit, not the host RAM
max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio of 0.9 applies to it
the remaining 10% is headroom so the OOM killer stays out

question: Why is memswap_limit set equal to mem_limit?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#6. A hard 3 GiB memory limit with no swap, and what ClickHouse does with it

key_facts.fact: memswap_limit is RAM plus swap, so equal values mean no swap
a database that swaps gets slow in a way that is hard to attribute

question: Why MergeTree and not ReplacingMergeTree for raw_swaps?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#10. Engine: MergeTree, with deduplication left to the load
docs/SCHEMA_EXPERIMENTS.md#2.4 MergeTree against ReplacingMergeTree

key_facts.fact: every reader would have to remember FINAL, or read about 10% too high
the materialized view counts a redelivered row twice whatever the engine, so the load must be idempotent
a duplicate that gets into a MergeTree stays, so a sanity check looks for duplicates

question: Why is block_timestamp in the sorting key right after pool_address?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#11. ORDER BY (pool_address, block_timestamp, block_number, log_index), PRIMARY KEY on the first two

key_facts.fact: with time in the key one day of the biggest pool reads 32,768 rows against 348,759 without it
pool goes first because there are only 4 distinct values

question: Why is the raw table partitioned by month?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#12. PARTITION BY month, for management and not for speed
docs/SCHEMA_OPTIONS.md#Recommendation (3)

key_facts.fact: partitioning is for data management, not speed; it changed no read
a month can be dropped, detached or replaced as a unit

question: Why are amount0 and amount1 stored as Int256?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#13. Types: lossless integers, and hashes and addresses in binary

key_facts.fact: a real swap of 1,136 WETH needs 70 bits so Int64 overflows
through Float64 a value loses wei without any error

question: Why are tx_hash and addresses stored as binary?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#13. Types: lossless integers, and hashes and addresses in binary

key_facts.fact: tx_hash as hex text was 52.9% of the table on disk and compressed 1.1x
binary made the table 30% smaller
a readable display needs hex() and a filter needs unhex()

question: Why is the pool label not copied into raw_swaps?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#14. Nothing from pools.yml is denormalised into the raw table

key_facts.fact: the raw table is a faithful copy of the chain and pools.yml stays the single source for hand-maintained facts
fixing a typo in a label would mean rewriting the table

question: Why does the reconciliation skip some pool-days?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#15. The external comparison only looks at days that are whole on both sides
docs/RECONCILIATION_FINDINGS.md#2. Partial days and open candles — EXPLAINED

key_facts.fact: it compares only days complete on our side, not the first or last day
the external candle must have been closed when downloaded
USDC/WETH 0.01% read -2.14% against an open candle and -0.55% once closed

question: When is a pool-day flagged in the reconciliation?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#16. A pool-day is flagged beyond 1% AND beyond 1,000 USD
docs/RECONCILIATION_FINDINGS.md#10. In thin pools a percentage alone does not discriminate — EXPLAINED

key_facts.fact: it is beyond 1% and also beyond 1,000 USD
a percentage alone flags tiny differences in the thin wstETH pools

question: Why is the external check GeckoTerminal and not the subgraph?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#17. The external check is GeckoTerminal, not the subgraph

key_facts.fact: it needs no API key so anyone can reproduce the reconciliation
it publishes no methodology, which is the tradeoff

question: Why must every read of the external daily volume table use FINAL?
relevant: docs/EXTERNAL_SOURCE.md#The table

key_facts.fact: it is a ReplacingMergeTree where the newest fetched_at wins only when parts merge
without FINAL a sum was twice the real figure

question: What can the agent_reader ClickHouse user do?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#19. A read-only user limited to the marts, for readers and agents
DECISIONS.md#21. The agent's guardrails: what the server enforces and what is code

key_facts.fact: it is readonly and has SELECT on five mart tables only
queries stop at 10 seconds, 10,000 result rows and 500,000,000 bytes of memory

question: Why is the read-only user opt-in on the real server?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#19. A read-only user limited to the marts, for readers and agents
docs/AGENT_ACCESS.md#Read this first: with the mount, the server will not start without the hash

key_facts.fact: a mounted file without its password hash stops the server from starting
it is started with make up-reader, and a plain make up recreates the container without it

question: Why is fct_pool_daily_smart_money empty in the fixture?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#20. The fixture carries no smart-money rows

key_facts.fact: a pool, a day and an amount identify a public transaction and through it the wallet Nansen classifies
Nansen's redistribution guidelines forbid publishing what can be traced to their classification
the fixture keeps the schema and no rows, so the honest answer is a refusal

question: Which agent guardrails does the server enforce and which are only code?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#21. The agent's guardrails: what the server enforces and what is code
docs/AGENT.md#Guardrails: what the server enforces and what is code

key_facts.fact: the server enforces read-only, the five tables and the time, row and memory limits
code enforces six model calls per question, 200 rows to the model and the grounding check

question: What happens when the agent reaches the cap of model calls?
relevant: docs/AGENT.md#How a question ends

key_facts.fact: the result is no_answer
the loop never builds an answer out of what it has seen

question: When does the agent send a request again?
relevant: docs/AGENT.md#How a question ends

key_facts.fact: only after an HTTP 429 or 529, which were not served
it waits the retry-after header, at most 60 seconds, and sends at most three times

question: What does an ungrounded answer mean?
relevant: docs/AGENT.md#3. An ungrounded answer is kept, and marked
DECISIONS.md#21. The agent's guardrails: what the server enforces and what is code

key_facts.fact: the submitted value is not a cell of a result of the last turn that ran a query
the answer is kept and marked, and the command exits with 1
grounded does not mean right

question: Why can the dollar budget stop a question with most of its money unspent?
relevant: docs/AGENT.md#1. The budget can stop a question with most of its money unspent

key_facts.fact: the worst case counts every byte of the request as one input token
the bound is loose, so with Opus or Sonnet only 2 or 3 of 6 calls were sent

question: What is the judge shown, and what does it return?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The judge: what code cannot check
DECISIONS.md#22. The judge is shown every query of the question

key_facts.fact: every query of the question with its rows, and the explanation
a verdict faithful or unfaithful through submit_verdict

question: Has the judge been calibrated against a person?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#Calibration: the judge against a person

key_facts.fact: no, the labels were written by a model, not a person
agreement is between two models and must not be described as human calibration

question: What tolerance does the evaluation give an amount of a token?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The tolerances, and why

key_facts.fact: relative only, 0.001, with no absolute bound
one unit of one token is worth very different amounts, so an absolute bound accepts almost anything for some

question: How are the evaluation cases split into dev and test?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The split

key_facts.fact: stratified by family, round(n / 3) to dev and the rest to test
fixed seed per family; 36 dev and 84 test of the 120 template cases
dev is for working on the prompt and test for the number reported

question: How much does a full baseline evaluation run cost and how long does it take?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#What a run costs: measured

key_facts.fact: about 0.31 USD for 180 cases
about 17 minutes

question: Did the refuse-early variant improve accuracy on test?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The one change measured: `refuse-early`, no measurable difference

key_facts.fact: no measurable difference: it fixed one case and broke one
accuracy on test went from 98.4% to 98.7%, inside the spread between runs

question: Does prompt caching lower the cost, and was it adopted?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#Prompt caching measured: cheaper, and not equivalent by the rule

key_facts.fact: cheaper: about 0.00109 USD per test question against 0.0017
not equivalent by the rule because refusals fell to 15 of 21 against a floor of 16
caching stays off and no cost reduction is claimed

question: Why did the gateway run of sonnet-ci end incomplete?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The same model through a gateway: the run is incomplete, and nothing is claimed

key_facts.fact: 8 of 53 questions ended in an error
HTTP 400, invalid signature in thinking block
the agent replays the reasoning block and the gateway does not support signed thinking-block replay

question: When does the evaluation check on a pull request fail?
relevant: docs/EVALS.md#The regression check on pull requests
DECISIONS.md#24. A regression check of the agent on pull requests

key_facts.fact: more than 3 of the 30 cases wrong
a case not asked, or a question that ended in an error
mean cost per question over 1.5 times the baseline

question: How many Nansen credits does the Free plan give?
relevant: docs/NANSEN.md#What runs today on the free tier

key_facts.fact: 100 one-time trial credits
then a daily top-up back to a 10-credit balance

question: Why was Nansen probed with USDC and not WETH?
relevant: docs/NANSEN.md#The probe, and why the token is USDC and not WETH

key_facts.fact: Nansen files ether under the native placeholder 0xeeee, not the WETH contract; WETH returned zero trades
USDC is a leg of all four pools

question: Why did the materialized view hold zero rows after it was created over existing data?
relevant: docs/MATERIALIZED_VIEW.md#The one thing to know
docs/WALKTHROUGH.md#4. The materialized view, and the mistake it invites (1 minute)

key_facts.fact: a materialized view is an insert trigger, not a stored query
rows already in the table are not in the target

question: What is the eth_getLogs block range limit on the free tier?
relevant: docs/MEASUREMENTS.md#Block range limit
README.md#Backfill

key_facts.fact: 10 blocks, inclusive, so toBlock minus fromBlock is 9
the rejection is HTTP 400 and is not retried

question: How is the price gap between the two USDC/WETH fee tiers computed?
relevant: docs/CROSS_POOL.md#Method

key_facts.fact: 10,000 times ln of the price ratio, in basis points
the price comes from sqrtPriceX96 and the other pool's price is joined with an ASOF JOIN
the fee band is 6 bps (1 + 5)

question: Why does the Airflow DAG use Airflow 3 and not 2.x?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#25. Airflow runs the daily pipeline, in a compose file of its own and outside the main dependencies

key_facts.fact: Airflow 2.x is end of life since 2026-04-22
a new pipeline on a series without security fixes would be the wrong thing to learn on

question: Why is the DAG limited to max_active_runs=1?
relevant: DECISIONS.md#25. Airflow runs the daily pipeline, in a compose file of its own and outside the main dependencies

key_facts.fact: every run appends to one landing zone that must be a single range
two days fetched at once could leave a gap and the load would refuse it

question: Does a projection ordered by time help the queries?
relevant: docs/QUERY_PERFORMANCE.md#2. A projection ordered by time

key_facts.fact: all pools for one day read 29% fewer rows
it costs a second full copy of the data, +100% on disk
one pool one day does not use it

question: Is the day boundary the cause of the differences with GeckoTerminal?
relevant: docs/RECONCILIATION_FINDINGS.md#3. The day boundary is not the cause — EXPLAINED (a negative result)

key_facts.fact: no: the distance is smallest at a shift of 0 h in all four pools
the source's candles start at 00:00:00 UTC, observed and not documented

question: How are stablecoins valued in the volume figures?
relevant: README.md#Limitations

key_facts.fact: a stablecoin is taken at exactly 1 USD
a pool without a stablecoin gets volume_usd NULL
